name: Shimron
overview: Shimron was a male member of the tribe of Issachar, identified specifically as a son of Issachar. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, highlighting his role in the early formation of the Israelite people. The Shimronites, a group descending from him, are noted in the biblical record, emphasizing his lasting tribal significance.
namesAndTitles: The name Shimron means 'guardian' or 'watchman,' reflecting a role of vigilance or protection. This proper name is recorded in Genesis 46:13 and is not indicated as being divinely given, but it carries a meaningful Hebrew root that underscores his tribal identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shimron as a son of Issachar, establishing his place within the family lineage of Israel. Beyond this paternal relationship, no additional family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shimron's significance lies in his place among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking the continuation of God's covenant people during a critical period of their history. His descendants, the Shimronites, are recognized in the census of Israel, indicating the enduring tribal structure God established. Through Shimron, the tribe of Issachar's heritage and God's providential preservation of Israel are underscored within the biblical narrative.
